source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
For good seed selection, farmers should choose:

- High-yielding varieties (modern/hybrid varieties, or pure/local varieties suited to the specific area).
- Seed with a growth duration and characteristics appropriate to the local geography and climate.
- Fresh seed that has not been stored for a long time.
- Pure seed lots, with purity exceeding 98%.
- Seed with a strong germination rate. The source text states a germination rate figure that reads as exceeding "85 to 900%" -- a germination rate over 100% is not possible, so this appears to be a printing/transcription error in the source (the intended figure was most likely around 90%), and the discrepancy is flagged here rather than silently corrected. A separate seed-moisture figure of about 13-14% is also given alongside this.
- Seeding rate: seed quantity used should be in the range of about 12 to 17 kilograms per hectare.
